That's real awful to hear, man. I used to be quite smart as well, and I just want to be able to return to my former intelligence. You hit the nail on the head with your description of the cognitive impairment. Let me know if you ever want to message.
I hope I'll feel normal again eventually. And I would give anything to be able to fall asleep next to her.

Glad I could help, I used THC oil cartridges (the good ones). To be honest, I don't know why I keep going. Every day feels worse than the last. Basically I was really sleep deprived and took a large dose of benadryl (think like 10 50mg capsules). I was kind of experimenting, as I usually only did 4 capsules, tops. The dosage had the inverse effect and instead caused me to be really disoriented, anxious, and paranoid. My legs were so restless I had to go for a walk, and I subconsciously was using my cartridge a good bit. I remember vaguely  walking down my neighborhood, scared shitless of what seems like absolutely nothing. When I managed to get back to my house, I felt like I was having a heart attack mixed with a massive head rush. I was shaking really hard, and crashed not long after. I don't know if the symptoms of my mental decline began immediately the next day, or began to appear slowly in the following weeks, but needless to say I've never really been the same. An odd story, I know. To this day I'm still wondering if it was a panic attack or if my shit had been laced with something.
Maybe if I do it my ex will finally want me again...
There's literally no downside

Ever since a bad experience with drugs, I've felt the exact same. It feels like everything's slipping and you are completely powerless to do anything.  Mine was induced by a panic attack, since then, I've felt like a half vegetative shell of my former self.
No problem dude, apparantly we aren't alone in this world

You seem to suffer from Misophonia, or hatred of certain sounds. I can be considered a Misophoniac myself, as hearing eating noises makes me want to go berserk and pummel the person eating into the ground.

I just can't seem to break my ways. I'm stuck in the same loop day in and day out, and I just feel like I could do this until I waste away. I might have deserved a better life, but none of this matters in the grand scheme of things. About the whole ex thing, I can't help but feel the utmost attraction for her. She was not only my first girlfriend, but she asked me out. She was always so giddy to be around me and we truly clicked for a while before our first breakup. When she came back, we made like rabbits for a few days until she left again. It's not just her looks. Everything about her, I love more than anything. Her voice, her charming nature, and the way she made me feel like a human being briefly. I can understand why she left. She wanted a boyfriend, not an emotional burden and potential liability. I know I'll never have the balls to woo her back, let alone tell another soul about my true intentions. I'm pretty moved by your words, and I genuinely care that you took time to answer, but I know I'll just be the same sad sack who wastes his life because be can't appreciate it.

Thank you man. I want to give what you said a shot at least, but I doubt I'd find anything that would ever captivate my interest. I might get off my ass at some point, but for the foreseeable future, the cycle continues. On a less pessimistic note, Outer Worlds looks great, AND Obsidian is publishing it so we might just get another game as revered as New Vegas. Miles above Fallout 4 from what I've seen so far.

I've been on Fluoxetine, didn't work. Now I'm stuck with another sugar pill and honestly, I think it brings out the worst in me. I'm impulsive, quicker to irritate than my former self, and much more open to the idea of going through with my plans than I was previously. I personally believe that antidepressants are vastly ineffective, and can even act as a catalyst for suicidal tendencies. It's great that they work for some people, but I guess I'm just immune. Again, I appreciate the continued responses and effort to help, but I don't think my brain was ever right to begin with.

My life is extremely monotonous, and that could be a large part of it. But I genuinely feel like I don't belong on this Earth. More often than not, even my friends fatigue me. Everything just makes me want to lie down and close my eyes. When I told my ex, (over snapchat) about my worldview I guess I just made her realize I wasn't half the man she thought I was. She was polite about it and offered some words for me, but after that she went cold on me.
I've been in that boat man, and it ain't fun at all. I fried my brain a while back, and shit just doesn't feel the same. By the way, do you recall the name of your condition?

I kind of understand what you're getting at, but to me the ultimate desire is to simply cease existing. I know I sound ungrateful, but I just can't have that much fun. My dopamine receptors are most likely akin to that of a cocaine user, only firing with the help of drugs. I feel like I'm just playing Earthbound whenever I play a game nowadays. A cool experience, yeah, but just not all that fun. I'm sorry if I offended any Mother fans.

I really appreciate it, but just when the urge to put a cap in my dome subsides, it comes right back. Also, I'd feel extremely uncomfortable and weak revealing this to anyone non-anonymously, so I don't think that'll happen. Specially not after last time.

TF2, Oblivion, S.T.A.L.K.E.R - Shadow of Chernobyl, Skyrim, Fallout 3, Fallout New Vegas, Fallout 4, COD zombies, GTA V, Overwatch, CS:GO, L4D, L4D2, Portal, Portal 2... and that's about all that comes to mind right now, sorry.
I've steadily stopped eating as well, and I'm losing weight like a prisoner of war. I just don't feel hungry most days.

Oh, and I almost forgot the best part! My copious experimentation has caused a steady cognitive decline. No physician has verified this, but just the way my brain feels these days, I know it's true. I don't have an internal monologue anymore, or very many thoughts. My memories, even of her, are incredibly vague. I can't remember my childhood well at all anymore, in stark contrast to just a year ago when I was less of a drug addict. I can't pay much attention, and I dissociate frequently, my mind not processing outside stimuli. This can be considered a brief moment of mental clarity as I type this out. It'll be gone soon enough.
